name: ai-dev-kit
description: Portable agentic-development skill library: lifecycle skills, a per-project adapter contract, and a cross-platform installer.

hooks.config: hooks/installer-hooks.json (installer form, ships to consumers as hooks.json) · hooks/hooks.json (plugin form, auto-discovered by the plugin loader; smoke-enforced parity)
hooks.policy: advise by default — hooks inject context; the agent decides. Blocking exists only behind the adapter's `enforcement` block (stop-gate · banned-api-guard · checkpoint-autorun), each handler inert until the project's user-owned config opts in

handlers.fires: package.json edits; pm add/update/upgrade or install-with-args commands
a file tool is about to edit .claude/skills/ or .claude/hooks/ directly — fires before the wasted edit lands
a Bash command writes to .claude/skills/ or .claude/hooks/ (sed -i, cp, mv, tee, a redirect) — the indirect edits the PreToolUse twin's Edit|Write matcher can't see
edits to AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md at any depth, files under the adapter docs.contextDir (default docs/context), or agent-memory files (~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/*.md)
a session resuming from context compaction — one-shot reorientation nudge (status doc + current row + re-verify assumed findings)

session end — runs the gate in the background via asyncRewake (turn ends immediately); a configured gate command failing exits 2, which wakes the agent one turn later with the failure; inert without adapter opt-in

session idle with a dirty tree or unpushed commits — blocks once for an autonomous checkpoint turn; loop-guarded (stop_hook_active + TTL lock), skips pending-question and mid-rebase/merge stops; inert without adapter opt-in
a file-tool edit landing a banned pattern under a guarded path (comment-stripped, line-based) — exit 2 blocks; inert without adapter opt-in

hooks.reviewedAgainst: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks — 33 documented events, full-surface pass 2026-08-24 (0.20.0), extended 2026-08-31 (2.1.251 added PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch, both rejected). Only 11 events can return hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext (SessionStart, Setup, SubagentStart, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Stop, SubagentStop); the other 22 can only block, act, or talk to the human, and the kit's default is advise-only (blocking exists solely behind the adapter enforcement opt-in). .github/smoke-hooks.mjs asserts this log covers the full surface.

reviewed.SessionStart: accepted 0.16.0 for the `compact` matcher only (compact-reorient) — compaction is the one entry point where disorientation is the default. `startup|resume|clear` rejected 0.16.0: a per-session nudge is latency and noise, and orientation on a normal start is the resume prompt's job. `fork` rejected 0.20.0: a forked session inherits its parent's context, so orientation is intact
reviewed.Setup: rejected 0.20.0 — fires only under `--init-only`, `-p --init`, or `-p --maintenance`, never on normal startup, so an orientation or drift nudge here would essentially never reach an interactive session; SessionStart already covers per-session entry
reviewed.InstructionsLoaded: rejected 0.20.0 — observability only: no additionalContext, no decision control, runs asynchronously. Nothing to advise with
reviewed.UserPromptSubmit: rejected 0.20.0 — accepts additionalContext but fires on every prompt; a standing nudge at that frequency is the same noise trade already rejected for SessionStart(startup). Facts that apply to every prompt belong in CLAUDE.md, which loads without running a script
reviewed.UserPromptExpansion: rejected 0.20.0 — matches skill/command names, but a kit skill's own SKILL.md already carries its rules; re-injecting them at expansion pays for the same content twice. PLAYBOOK #9: the skill trigger already covers it
reviewed.MessageDisplay: rejected 0.20.0 — display-only. `displayContent` rewrites what the human sees while the transcript and the model keep the original text, so it cannot advise the agent
reviewed.PreToolUse: accepted 0.2.0 — live-verify-reminder (matcher Bash, if: "Bash(git *)"): fires before a commit, the last moment the agent can still run the verify recipe. 0.23.19 adds skill-drift-guard-preedit (matcher Edit|Write): fires before a direct edit to .claude/skills/ or .claude/hooks/ lands, so the redirect-to-kit-source precedes the wasted edit instead of following it
reviewed.PermissionRequest: rejected 0.20.0 — decision-only (`decision.behavior` allow/deny) with no context channel; auto-answering a permission prompt is a block-class action the kit's trust contract excludes
reviewed.PostToolUse: accepted 0.2.0 — dep-check-nudge, skill-drift-guard, context-guard: the tool result is the moment the agent can still act on what it just did. 0.23.0 adds banned-api-guard on the same event — opt-in blocking (adapter enforcement.bannedApis), inert without config. 0.23.19 narrows skill-drift-guard's matcher to Bash only — its Edit|Write coverage moved to the PreToolUse twin (skill-drift-guard-preedit), so this handler now catches only the indirect Bash-command edits the pre-edit matcher can't see
reviewed.PostToolUseFailure: rejected 0.20.0 — accepts additionalContext and checkpoint's three-strikes rule is the natural payload, but strike counting needs cross-call state a stateless handler cannot hold, and firing on every tool error (a typo'd grep, a missing file) is an intolerable false-positive rate. Revisit only with a session state file
reviewed.PostToolBatch: rejected 0.20.0 — fires once per batch with the full tool set, but supports no matcher; the kit's three PostToolUse nudges are per-file and per-command decisions that need exactly the matcher scoping this event cannot express, and there is no batch-level fact worth injecting on its own
reviewed.PermissionDenied: rejected 0.20.0 — `retry` only, no context channel; re-driving a denied tool call is the user's decision, not a hook's
reviewed.Notification: rejected 0.20.0 — a user-facing surface (permission prompts, idle, auth, elicitation dialogs) with no context channel to the agent
reviewed.SubagentStart: rejected 0.20.0 — can inject context into a spawning subagent, but no kit invariant is subagent-specific: the one real risk, a subagent editing `.claude/skills/` directly, is already caught by skill-drift-guard's PreToolUse/PostToolUse twins, which fire for subagent tool calls too. A generic per-spawn nudge is the SessionStart(startup) noise trade again
reviewed.SubagentStop: rejected 0.20.0 — feedback loops back into a subagent that has finished; the parent-side equivalent is a PostToolUse hook on the Agent tool, which is already the kit's wired event
reviewed.TaskCreated: rejected 0.20.0 — cancel/block only; no context channel, and cancelling a task is a block
reviewed.TaskCompleted: rejected 0.20.0 — exit-2 or `continue: false` blocking only; the kit's hooks advise, never block
reviewed.Stop: partial 0.23.0 — accepted behind explicit adapter enforcement opt-in only: stop-gate (the session may not end with the project's fast gate red) and checkpoint-autorun (one autonomous checkpoint turn when idle with pending work), both inert without `enforcement` config. Reverses the 0.20.0 rejection on consumer evidence via retro: next-web-boilerplate ran checkpoint-autorun and danger-noodles/smash-gods/wyrd ran stop-gates in production sessions, and none of the predicted every-turn noise materialized because the handlers fire on state (red gate, pending work), not on every stop. The unconfigured default remains rejected — no nag ships without the project's recorded choice
reviewed.StopFailure: rejected 0.20.0 — matches API and transport error classes (rate_limit, overloaded, billing_error); no context channel, and nothing project-shaped to advise about
reviewed.TeammateIdle: rejected 0.20.0 — blocking-shaped (exit 2 / `continue: false`) and scoped to teammate sessions the kit does not model
reviewed.ConfigChange: rejected 0.20.0 — the `skills` matcher looked like the gap-closer for `.claude/skills/` mutated outside the file tools, but the event has no additionalContext: it can only block, and a blocked change surfaces no message to the user or to Claude (debug log only). A silent block is the exact opposite of advise-never-block; `install.mjs --check` remains the drift guard
reviewed.CwdChanged: rejected 0.20.0 — returns `watchPaths` and `systemMessage` only, and the systemMessage is a terminal notification that does not reach the model
reviewed.DirectoryAdded: rejected 0.20.0 — with the `slash_command` matcher its systemMessage does reach Claude on the next turn, so a context channel exists, but `/add-dir` is rare and nothing in the kit's lifecycle keys off it. Reconsider if a multi-root workflow lands
reviewed.FileChanged: rejected 0.20.0 — a filesystem watcher that catches changes no tool matcher sees, genuinely attractive for skill and adapter drift, but it has no additionalContext and its systemMessage does not reach the SDK message stream. It can act on files or notify the human; it cannot advise the agent
reviewed.WorktreeCreate: rejected 0.20.0 — the contract is a worktree path on stdout and a failure fails creation; not an advisory surface
reviewed.WorktreeRemove: rejected 0.20.0 — teardown notification with no context channel
reviewed.PreCompact: rejected 0.16.0, re-verified 0.20.0 — the event cannot inject additionalContext (it is a top-level `decision` event); the accepted mechanism is SessionStart(compact)
reviewed.PostCompact: rejected 0.20.0 — the newer twin of PreCompact, with no decision control and no additionalContext at all; SessionStart(compact) remains the only mechanism for compact reorientation
reviewed.SessionEnd: rejected 0.20.0 — the session is over: no context channel and no turn left in which the agent could act
reviewed.Elicitation: rejected 0.20.0 — answers MCP form prompts on the agent's behalf (accept/decline/cancel), automating a human decision that SECURITY.md's trust contract puts out of scope
reviewed.ElicitationResult: rejected 0.20.0 — the same MCP elicitation surface after the response; overriding submitted form content is out of scope for the same reason
reviewed.PreModelSwitch: rejected 2.1.251 — decision-only (allow/deny a model switch), no additionalContext channel; blocking a model switch is out of scope for an advisory kit
reviewed.PostModelSwitch: rejected 2.1.251 — display-only notification that a switch occurred, no context channel back to the agent

contrarian.install: copy-once templates the project then owns — never touched by install.mjs or --check; agent → .claude/agents/, hook → .claude/hooks/ (repo-owned dir, not hooks/ai-dev-kit/)
contrarian.purpose: plan-gate dissent: a standing devil's-advocate subagent plus a sign-off nudge; consumer-proven in next-web-boilerplate and civicmatch before upstreaming

skills.name: checkpoint
skills.summary: Commit + push pending work, judge context health (three strikes on a repeated obstacle = unhealthy), then continue or hand off via an on-disk resume prompt plus a relaunch model × effort recommendation.

automation.active: Stop → hooks/checkpoint-autorun.mjs — opt-in (adapter enforcement.checkpointAutorun): one autonomous checkpoint turn when idle with pending work
automation.reviewed: Step 2 rejection ('a Stop-hook nag would be noise') reversed 0.23.0 via retro on next-web-boilerplate's consumer evidence — the hook fires on pending-work state, not every stop; default (no adapter opt-in) remains un-automated

skills.name: doc-audit
skills.summary: Keep docs, agent context, persistent memory, and showcase docs accurate and token-lean; archive instead of delete; enforce standing-instruction budgets and cache-stable placement (hunt 7).

skills.name: project-audit
skills.summary: Score every feature group /100 against a best-available bar; verify docs ↔ code; emit a prioritized backlog.
triggers: what's missing to make this perfect

skills.name: tidy
skills.summary: Prune the unbounded local build/engine cache; surface (never auto-run) orphaned dev processes, stale test data, dangling container images — per-stack recipes in references/.

automation.existing: cache prune at checkpoint + pre-push backstop
automation.reviewed: Step 2: no Claude hook — the existing cadence already covers it

skills.name: dep-check
skills.summary: Registry-verify a dependency before adding/upgrading: real version, tags, release-age window, pin policy, peers, standing holds — per-ecosystem registry recipes in references/.

automation.active: PostToolUse (Edit|Write|Bash) → hooks/dep-check-nudge.mjs — injects the dep-check reminder on package.json edits / pm installs

skills.name: live-verify
skills.summary: Full gate, then a fresh production-shaped run (served build · game export · CLI binary · packed library · sample pipeline slice), then drive the affected flow and observe real output — per-domain mechanics in references/.

composition.defersTo: project verify/run skill (harness built-ins bootstrap one)

automation.active: PreToolUse (Bash, if git *) → hooks/live-verify-reminder.mjs — injects the live-verify reminder before commits

skills.name: project-init
skills.summary: One-time inception: plan docs or a raw idea → discovery (gaps, value-adds, competitive scan, foundation fit-map) → one batched question round → product brief + regenerated status/backlog to a 100 bar → sign-off → the pipeline begins.
triggers: here's my idea for an app
turn these plan docs into a build plan

composition.precedes: the whole pipeline — the one-time entry point for a new project
composition.scoredBy: project-audit (against the brief's feature groups + bar)

automation.reviewed: 0.4.0: no hook — a post-scaffold nudge belongs in the template's getting-started text, not machinery; the skill triggers cover invocation

skills.name: project-adopt
skills.summary: One-time brownfield inception: an existing codebase → product survey doubling as the parity contract (incoming agentic layer included) → theirs-vs-foundation disposition map under a two-tiered meaningful-improvement bar (product surface defaults keep-theirs; foundation tier defaults the target's) → data/user reality check → one batched question round → product brief + migration map with recorded comparisons + regenerated status/backlog whose completion is a surface-identical app on the target foundation, parity proven by test suites at the adopting repo's thresholds → sign-off → the pipeline begins.
triggers: port my app onto the template
migrate an existing app to this boilerplate
merge the boilerplate into my app
upgrade my app with the template's features

composition.consumes: the existing codebase — arg path/git URL or the adapter init.sourceDir drop dir; a read-only, never-committed reference
feeds: upstream candidates (template issues/PRs; keep-theirs rows double as template lessons)
composition.precedes: the whole pipeline — the one-time entry point for an existing product; the parity check becomes the standing live-verify mode for port rows
composition.scoredBy: project-audit (against the brief's feature groups + bar)

automation.reviewed: 0.6.0: no hook — same rationale as project-init; the template's getting-started text and the skill triggers cover invocation

skills.name: harness-audit
skills.summary: Periodic currency audit of the agent harness itself: inventory the local surface (skills/hooks/context files/tool servers/permissions/packaging), re-fetch the pinned authoritative specs (self-repairing references/sources.md), sweep the ecosystem with current-dated category queries (maintaining references/stack.md), diff against the rubric, and emit a dated scored report + proposed backlog rows. Report-only; sign-off gates implementation.
triggers: is our agent setup still current

composition.siblingOf: project-audit (product) · doc-audit (docs) — this one audits the agentic layer
composition.consumes: the skill linter's and eval runner's mechanical results where present (eval presence is scored from the graded pass, not fixture existence); prior HARNESS_AUDIT reports (diff-bounded)

automation.reviewed: 0.16.0: no hook, no scheduler — a calendar nudge would fire without regard to program state; the status doc's periodic-pass line and the skill triggers cover cadence

skills.name: retro
skills.summary: Post-milestone compounding harvest: corrections, surprises, re-derivations, and repeated manual steps routed to the cheapest durable home (memory · instruction line · adapter field · skill edit · hook candidate · test), each behind the normal sign-off gate; rejections recorded so lessons aren't re-litigated.
triggers: what should we learn from this
make sure this doesn't happen again

automation.reviewed: 0.16.0: no Stop/session-end hook — a retro nag after every session would be noise; checkpoint's three-strikes suggestion plus the skill triggers cover it
